Provenance-verification slice: compiled skill rules T-51 through T-75 of .claude/skills/tdd-bdd/. Repo /home/user/BookMinder, branch claude/bookminder-recall-5ite2s. Format+method reference (follow its verdict-table format exactly): .coordination/compile/provenance-verification-P12-P14.md.

For each rule in your range:
1. Resolve and read sources: `source .venv/bin/activate; python3 .coordination/tools/rule.py -r T-NN -c 60` from repo root — prints raw corpus fragments plus numbered transcript windows around every cited day-NNN:LNNN loc. Watch stderr for unresolved ids. A corpus id may exist in BOTH .coordination/mining/v2/ and .coordination/mining/pairing/ as DISTINCT entries — verify each separately. The rule-index may use alias suffixes (e.g. p021t-R2 means pairing/day-021.yaml's p021-R2). Non-corpus sources (ledger L-NN, CLAUDE.md:line, threads.md rulings, brief-mandate) are OUT OF SCOPE — mark them so; they are author-ratified.
2. Judge each corpus source against its transcript window, never against the YAML summary alone: QUOTE (character-exact at cited loc), EPISODE (does because/what-happened match the actual exchange; distortion subtypes seen so far: embellished-because, misattribution), GENERALIZATION (does the rule follow from the episode, or overreach — episode-specific instruction universalized — or dropped-qualifier), MISSED CONTEXT (material shortly before/after that changes the lesson, e.g. a later reversal). Verdict per source: FAITHFUL | DISTORTED(subtype) | OVERREACH(how) | UNDERREACH(what missed).
3. Per-rule ROLL-UP: does the compiled wording capture what its scenarios actually taught? Where it does not, propose a concrete rewording / split / standalone rule, grounded in the windows you read (cite day:loc). Do NOT edit the skill — a downstream judge applies changes.

DELIVERABLE: .coordination/compile/provenance-verification-tdd-bdd-3.md — verdict table (rule | source | quote | episode | generalization | missed-context | verdict), short notes only for non-FAITHFUL rows, then roll-ups ONLY for rules where you propose a change. Never hard-wrap prose (one line per bullet/paragraph; tables exempt). No praise, no meta-narration. Commit ONLY that file, push -u origin claude/bookminder-recall-5ite2s (retry 4x, backoff 2/4/8/16s, network errors only).

RETURN (max 10 lines): verdict counts, non-FAITHFUL ids with one-word reasons, count of rules with change proposals, commit SHA.

33	## Notes on non-FAITHFUL entries
34	
35	**p003-R7 — UNDERREACH.** The mined rule stops at "which durable home does X get: a CLAUDE.md rule or a toolchain setting". The window shows the agent answering that question three times over in one turn: one CLAUDE.md line (L1808-L1814, which survived), a new 124-line `docs/pre-commit-workflow.md` (L1818-L1828), and a `fix-and-stage.sh` helper script (L1831-L1842). The author rejected the chmod (L1847) and criticized the doc as "something that you wanted to tell me in Claude Code console output" (L1850). The episode therefore carries a second, tighter lesson the entry drops: the durable home is the smallest existing one, and manufacturing a new document or script to hold a one-line lesson is the same evaporation failure wearing a diff. Any P-14 revision that leans on p003-R7 should carry that qualifier, or it will license exactly the artifact-inflation this episode ended in.
36	
37	**p013-R7 — DISTORTED.** The `because` reads "The author explicitly demanded comprehension, not compliance, before letting the rule be written into the constitution." Nothing in the window concerns writing to CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md; the demand at L1597-L1603 gates a *commit*, and the agent's reply is a three-point explanation, not a rules-file diff. The distortion inflates the episode into a constitution-amendment gate it never was. The episode's actual force is the opposite direction and stronger: at L1647-L1650 the author corrected the reasoning the agent had restated — the emoji was to be kept, and the dual Pro/Flash attribution was a specific historical credit from day-011, not a general standard. Two of three restated reasons were wrong, and the restatement is what made that visible. `because_source: user-verbatim` overstates: the quote is verbatim, the `because` is not.
38	
39	**p021-R8 v2 — DISTORTED.** The `because` claims "the author enumerated all of them" for the list-recent story, the filter story, the implementation and two doc sections. He did not. At L7068-L7070 he names the time-control problem and then issues a general directive to "review our stories, scenatios and implementations for consistency". The enumeration appears at L7181-L7184 in the agent's own TodoWrite, after the fact. What the author did do — twice — is catch specific stale text the agent had left behind (L7113, L7124). The rule survives the correction, but its evidentiary weight is "the agent's sweep was incomplete twice and the author caught it", not "the author supplied the invalidation list".
40	
41	## Roll-up (a) — P-12 and the pending revision
42	
43	P-12 as compiled reads: *Account for everything in the tree. When a file appears that no requirement produced, surface it yourself before the partner finds it; when asked to change something, change it in place — never a parallel copy alongside the original.* All four sources verify clean at the episode level, and two of them (p018-R9, p021-R2) map directly onto the second clause; the parallel-copy prohibition is the best-evidenced sentence in the rule, attested in two independent sessions with two different failure shapes — a rejected `*_improved` file and a committed `*_v2` spec.
44	
45	The **census trigger** is supported in substance but not in the periodic form. The author never asked for a periodic sweep; he ran five audits himself, and the mined "periodically census" is agent-synthesized mechanism sitting under a `because_source: user-verbatim` label. What the transcripts do show is that every audit follows a structural event: an editable install producing `bookminder.egg-info` (day-002:L1842), a bulk directory cleanup (L1131), a tooling/pre-commit batch (L2792), and — in day-021 — a parallel spec file that survived a commit before being caught (L1288). The evidence supports an event-triggered census (after any install, scaffold, tooling change, or before a commit), not a cadence. A revision that writes "periodically" imports a mechanism no episode attests; a revision that names the triggering events is fully carried by the corpus.
46	
47	The **rejected-edit clause** is supported and overdue. p004-R11 is currently listed as a merged source for P-12 while none of its content appears in the compiled sentence — the rule as written has nothing to say about a diff that was proposed and refused. The episode verifies exactly: the author could not tell whether the hatchling change had reached disk and had to ask (day-004:L487), and needed a second turn (L494) to learn that rejected diffs are never written. The clause belongs in P-12 because it is the same obligation — the state of the tree is yours to account for, including the parts of it you did *not* change. Two precisions from the transcript: the agent's answer was correct, so the clause is about volunteering file state unprompted rather than about correcting an error; and the entry is classed `reciprocal` in the corpus while P-12 is a mirror rule, which is defensible here (it is a claim about your own tree, not a check on the partner) but should be a deliberate call, not an accident of merging.
48	
49	Verdict on the revision: the full verified evidence supports both additions, with one correction — drop "periodically" in favour of the structural triggers the episodes actually share.

51	## Roll-up (b) — P-14 and the over-merge question
52	
53	P-14 as compiled carries three clauses: second-correction to durable repair in the same turn; retract every copy and correct the record; revert a wrong rule rather than patching around it. Fourteen entries are merged into it, but they are not fourteen independent episodes — p006-R3 and d006-R15 are the same author turn at day-006:L2511 split across two corpus files, so the apparent support for the retraction clause is one episode, not two. Clause coverage is otherwise real: p002-R4 and p003-R7 and p011-R11 carry clause 1, p006-R3/d006-R15 and p014-R5 and p021-R8-v2 carry clause 2, p002-R7 carries clause 3, and p005-R5 is the source of the "your future carefulness is not a mechanism" because.
54	
55	On the four entries under question:
56	
57	**p013-R7 — deserves standalone expression.** Nothing in P-14 asks you to restate the reasoning behind a correction in your own words, and nothing invites the partner to correct the reasoning rather than the output. The episode shows why the move earns its own rule: the restatement was wrong on two of three points and the author caught it *because* the reasoning was on the table (day-013:L1647-L1650). By P-14's own logic — a rule that ends as advice evaporates — a rule written down but misunderstood is not a mechanism either, so this is a complement to P-14, not a sub-case of it. It is a mirror move.
58	
59	**p018-R3 — deserves standalone expression, or P-14's verb must change.** P-14 says "propose the durable repair". The episode is the failure of proposing: "Noted." at day-018:L1243, then "Should I add this rule to CLAUDE.md?" at L1269, with three author prompts before the rule reached even a todo item. The specifics the merge dropped — write it in the same turn, name the file and section, never answer "Noted." — are the observable part; "propose" is not falsifiable in the same way. The same failure recurs at day-002:L1228 and day-021:L1722 ("Please remember that", never written), so this is a three-session pattern, not one incident. Strengthening P-14's clause 1 from "propose" to "write, and name the file and section" would carry it; a standalone rule would carry it more visibly.
60	
61	**p021-R8 — the question rests on a mis-identified entry.** "Commit inferior-then-improved" is `pairing/day-021.yaml` p021-R8 @ day-021:L1722, dispositioned to P-26, and P-26 does express it ("consider committing the inferior version first so the diff between the two carries the reasoning"). It is not in P-14 and was not over-merged there. The entry that *is* merged into P-14 is `v2/day-021.yaml` p021-R8 @ day-021:L7069, whose lesson is a consistency sweep after new evidence invalidates prior claims. P-14's clause 2 is framed around retracting *a claim*; this episode is wider — one discovery invalidated stories, scenarios, an implementation and two doc sections at once. That is an underreach of a word, not a missing rule: clause 2 should read as sweeping every artifact that repeats an invalidated claim, whether the trigger was your retraction or new evidence.
62	
63	**p003-R13 — deserves standalone expression, and not in mirror.md.** It is dispositioned to P-28 with "(part)" credited to P-14, but neither compiled text expresses it. P-28 is "Teach when asked why"; P-14 is about your own repeated corrections. Nothing in either says: when the partner names a process failure of his own, extract the mechanism, and do not console him or reframe the loss as an investment. The evidence is unusually clean — the author's self-assessment at day-003:L2305 and the agent's verbatim "Consider it an investment rather than procrastination!" at L2320 — and the move is reciprocal, about how you receive the partner's self-criticism, so it belongs in reciprocal.md rather than as a P-14 clause.
64	
65	One entry outside the question deserves the same scrutiny: **p002-R10** (apply a named principle to every instance it covers; report the full sweep, day-002:L1096) verifies clean and is likewise absent from P-14's text. It, p021-R8-v2, and p006-R3/d006-R15 are three shapes of one sweep obligation — sweep after a correction, sweep after new evidence, sweep after a retraction — which suggests the clean revision is a single explicit sweep clause in P-14 rather than three implicit ones.
66	
67	Provenance flags carried by this pass, none of which change a verdict: `because_source: user-verbatim` labels an agent-synthesized `because` in p018-R9, p013-R7 and p021-R8-v2; p006-R3 prescribes a grep that no episode attests; p012-R7's `because` quotes a composite phrasing that appears verbatim in no turn; p011-R11's second `because` clause lies outside the verified window; and p014-R5 rests entirely on agent self-narration with no author turn in the window — it codifies behavior the agent performed correctly rather than a correction the author made.

## Roll-ups

### T-53 — split the fixture-coupling rule from the FIXME mechanism

T-53 currently reads: *Never weaken an assertion to make it pass against the fixture you happen to have, and never repair an unconditionally-true assertion by hardcoding a fixture-derived number — when the only available assertion would couple to incidental fixture shape, mark FIXME naming the right technique and owning layer, and move on.* The first two clauses are the durable part and are enforced twice in the window (day-020:L2566 blocked, L2573 blocked). The trailing clause should be cut or rewritten, because the episode ends without a FIXME and with the author retracting the technique he had named.

Proposed wording: *Never weaken an assertion to make it pass against the fixture you happen to have, and never repair an unconditionally-true assertion by hardcoding a fixture-derived number. When the property you want to pin is not this layer's to pin, say which layer owns it and leave the spec asserting only what this layer can falsify — the limit belongs to whichever spec controls the volume, not to a count copied out of the fixture.* That is what day-020:L2605 actually decided, and it removes the invitation to leave a FIXME naming a technique that may be wrong.

### T-54 and T-59 — point the fix-the-fixture clauses at T-76

Both rules send the reader to the fixture and stop. Two independent sessions show the author interrupting at exactly that step (day-015:L2200, day-018:L1308), in both cases because the agent was about to hand-author fixture data. Minimal change: in T-54 replace "fix the fixture to contain it" with "fix the fixture to contain it, by copying the real record (T-76) rather than authoring one", and in T-59 replace "fix the fixture first" with "fix the fixture first, by copying from the real source (T-76)". No new rule is needed; the cross-reference is the whole fix.

### T-56 — carry the author's emphasized clause

Proposed wording: *Before rewriting or replacing an existing spec, recover why it exists — `git log -S` the construct and read the change that introduced it — and enumerate the properties it constrains, then show the replacement constrains each one; if it does not, say so instead of proposing the edit.* Grounded at day-020:L56044-L56046 (the instruction) and L56057-L56085 (the agent carrying it out). This is the same obligation T-23 states for declarations; stating it here is what makes it reachable from the page a spec rewrite sends you to.

### T-59 — third clause: name the real mechanism, and sweep

The third clause should stop saying the bad datum was invented. Proposed: *Before asserting on specific data, run the product against the fixture and read the actual output — an assertion carried over from an older fixture, or copied from a neighbouring spec, names data the fixture no longer contains; when you find one, grep the tree and fix the story cards and docs that carry the same stale datum.* Both halves are in the window: the stale reference lived in `specs/cli_spec.py` and `stories/discover/handle-user-environments.yaml` (day-018:L526-L534), and the author had to ask for the second one separately at L540 ("don't forget to also update the one in `stories`").

### T-61 — re-source, and mark the boundary against T-70

T-61 rests on one entry that verifies (d011-R10) and one that does not (d020s5-R5). The rule survives on d011-R10 alone, but the surviving evidence is a code listing with no author turn: nobody in the corpus ever objected to the absolute-path assertion, and the agent that wrote it (day-011:L3650-L3654) was rewriting an assertion to match observed output at the time. Two changes worth making: drop d020s5-R5 as a source, and add the distinction that keeps T-61 from being read against T-70 — *assert the sentinel your own double injected; never the real wording or real path the layer below produces.* Without it, T-61 ("no full internal message text in acceptance assertions") and T-70 ("the messages are passed throug") read as a conflict.

### T-62 — add the equal-strength case

Proposed wording: *Delete a spec that a stronger spec already subsumes, and when two specs constrain the same behavior with equal strength, keep the one whose motivation you can state; then sweep the file for other instances of the same redundancy — whole-output equality already pins ordering, content, and absence, so the weaker check adds maintenance without falsifying power, and redundancy comes in clusters.* The added clause is day-020:L14591 applied to L14576-L14583, and it is the only one of T-62's four sources that is a distinct episode rather than a re-rendering of the L2257 turn.
